problem:
From top to bottom, fill in the blanks and hence complete the proof of the following statement using the axioms $[\text{A}1]-[\text{A}8]$ given below.

*Given any $x\in V$, if $w$ is a vector such that $x+w=0$, then $w=-x$* 

*Proof:*

$$
\begin{aligned}x+w & =0 &  & [\,\text{given}\,] \\ (x+w)+(-x) & =0+(-x) &  & [\,\text{add }-x\text{ to both sides}\,] \\ (w+x)+(-x) & =(-x)+0 &  & [\,\text{axiom A1}\,] \\ (w+x)+(-x) & =-x &  & [\,\text{axiom A3}\,] \\ w+(x+(-x)) & =-x &  & [\,\text{axiom __}\,\,] \\ w+0 & =-x &  & [\,\text{axiom A4}\,] \\ w & =-x &  & [\,\text{axiom __}\,\,]\end{aligned}
$$

The axioms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{[A1]}:x+y=y+x & \text{[A5]}:1\cdot x=x \\ \text{[A2]}:(x+y)+z=x+(y+z) & \text{[A6]}:\alpha (\beta x)=(\alpha \beta )x \\ \text{[A3]}:x+0=x & \text{[A7]}:(\alpha +\beta )x=\alpha x+\beta x \\ \text{[A4]}:x+(-x)=0 & \text{[A8]}:\alpha (x+y)=\alpha x+\alpha y\end{aligned}
$$

examples.problem:
From top to bottom, fill in the blanks and hence complete the proof of the following statement using the axioms $[\textrm A1] - [\textrm A8]$ given below.

*Statement: *

*If $\mathbf{w}$ is a vector such that $\mathbf{w}+\mathbf{w} = \mathbf{w}$, then $\mathbf{w}=\mathbf{0}.$* 

*Proof:*

$$
\begin{aligned}w+w & =w &  & [\,\text{given}\,] \\ (w+w)+(-w) & =w+(-w) &  & [\,\text{add [math]-\mathbf{w}[/math] to both sides}\,] \\ w+(w+(-w)) & =w+(-w) &  & [\,\text{axiom __}\,\,] \\ w+0 & =0 &  & [\,\text{axiom A4}\,] \\ w & =0 &  & [\,\text{axiom __}\,\,]\end{aligned}
$$

The axioms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{[A1]}:x+y=y+x & \text{[A5]}:1\cdot x=x \\ \text{[A2]}:(x+y)+z=x+(y+z) & \text{[A6]}:\alpha (\beta x)=(\alpha \beta )x \\ \text{[A3]}:x+0=x & \text{[A7]}:(\alpha +\beta )x=\alpha x+\beta x \\ \text{[A4]}:x+(-x)=0 & \text{[A8]}:\alpha (x+y)=\alpha x+\alpha y\end{aligned}
$$
examples.worked_solution:
Using the axioms of a vector space, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}w+w & =w &  & [\,\text{given}\,] \\ (w+w)+(-w) & =w+(-w) &  & [\,\text{add [math]-\mathbf{w}[/math] to both sides}\,] \\ w+(w+(-w)) & =w+(-w) &  & [\,\text{axiom [math]{\color{blue}\text{A2}}[/math]}\,] \\ w+0 & =0 &  & [\,\text{axiom A4}\,] \\ w & =0 &  & [\,\text{axiom [math]{\color{blue}\text{A3}}[/math]}\,]\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Let $K$ be the set of all $2\times 1$ matrices $[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}],$ such that $x,y\in R$ and $x+y=1.$  Complete the following sentence:

*$K$ is **not** a vector space (with respect to matrix addition and scalar multiplication) because $\text{_________}\,.$*
feedback.worked_solution:
The correct answer is as follows:

*$K$ is **not** a vector space (with respect to matrix addition and scalar multiplication) because **the $2\times 1$  zero matrix does not belong to $K.$** *  

Indeed, adding the entries of the $2\times 1$  zero matrix yields $0+0=0\ne 1.$

On the other hand:

- addition of matrices is associative. $\,✓$

- addition and scalar multiplication of matrices  satisfy the distributive laws. $✓$

- Addition of matrices  is commutative. $\,✓$

- $1\cdot A=A$ for all $A\in K.$ $\,✓$

submitted_fields.submitted_value: the $2\times 1$  zero matrix does not belong to $K$
